summary: The note describes how high school students in a local community have launched recycling programs, starting with Lincoln High School's 'Lincoln Recycles' in September 2023. The effort grew through partnerships, other schools' campaigns, a recycling app, and a community fair, and it eventually prompted city legislation proposed to support such efforts. The students are now documenting their methods to share with other communities.
one_line: High school students, starting with Lincoln High's 'Lincoln Recycles', built community recycling programs that spread across the city and influenced local policy.
key_facts: Lincoln High School students led by Sarah Martinez started the 'Lincoln Recycles' program in September 2023 after noticing the amount of waste generated during lunch hours.
The Lincoln Recycles philosophy was to educate students about recycling, motivate them to act, and provide the means to do so.
By October 15, 2023, Sarah Martinez and her team had conducted several workshops and presented in classrooms about waste management.
By November 2023, Lincoln Recycles had partnerships with local businesses, environmental NGOs, and the municipal waste management department.
Jackson High School launched its 'Eco-Warriors' campaign in early December 2023, led by junior David Chen and his committee, with a neighborhood-wide recycling drive involving residents.
In January 2024, Kennedy High School students, including Emily Liu, developed a smartphone app teaching recycling dos and don'ts.
The Kennedy High School app tracks the nearest recycling bins and provides pickup services for large recyclable items.
The first annual 'Recycle Fest', organized by students from several high schools, took place on March 22, 2024.
Recycle Fest featured live music, educational booths, recycled art displays, and a recycled fashion show, and drew large crowds and local media attention.
On April 10, 2024, city council member Alex Johnson proposed legislation supporting community-based recycling efforts and recognizing high school students as key stakeholders.
The students have begun documenting their processes, challenges, and successes, and hold workshops and webinars to share their blueprint with schools around the world.
